description:
Both panels are schematic line plots illustrating how a quantity evolves over a streaming index \(m\) on the horizontal axis. In both plots, the x-axis is labeled \(m\), uses a linear scale, starts at 0 at the origin, and extends to the right with an arrow; a specific position \(m_0\) is indicated by a vertical dashed line down to the x-axis (no regular numeric tick spacing is shown beyond the origin and the labeled \(m_0\)).

In the top plot, the y-axis is labeled \(n\) with a linear scale and shows reference labels at 0 (at the origin), \(w\) (above 0), and two higher annotated levels labeled \(c-a-s\) and \(c-a\); dashed horizontal guide lines are drawn at the heights corresponding to \(c-a-s\) and \(c-a\). A single black solid line without markers forms a repeating sawtooth pattern: it begins at \((m=0, n=0)\), rises linearly to a peak aligned with the upper dashed line labeled \(c-a\), then drops nearly vertically to a lower level near the labeled \(w\), after which it rises linearly again to a similar peak and repeats this rise-and-drop behavior multiple times across increasing \(m\). To the right of the marked \(m_0\), the same black sawtooth continues with more frequent cycles, with peaks drawn around the mid-to-upper region (near the dashed reference heights) and troughs returning toward the lower region near \(w\).

In the bottom plot, the y-axis is labeled \(\mathrm{Size}_{\mathrm{run}}^{a}\) (as typeset on the left) on a linear scale, with 0 at the origin and higher annotated reference levels labeled \(w+a+s\) and \(c\); dashed horizontal guide lines are drawn at the heights corresponding to \(w+a+s\) and \(c\). A single black solid line without markers again forms a repeating sawtooth: it starts at \((m=0, y=0)\), increases linearly up to a peak that aligns with the dashed line labeled \(c\), then drops nearly vertically to a lower value around the dashed line labeled \(w+a+s\), and repeats this ramp-to-\(c\) then drop-to-\(w+a+s\) pattern across the x-axis. Past the vertical dashed line at \(m_0\), the sawtooth cycles continue with closely spaced ramps and drops, with peaks consistently returning to the level marked \(c\) and troughs returning toward the level marked \(w+a+s\).
